executiveAssessment.text:
Executive Conclusion. Falls Church Marriott Fairview Park's priority is a Reality Gap in how a distinctive part of the proposition is represented in AI answers.

What the Data Is Telling Us. Scenario Presence at 97.9% shows broad recognition across monitored traveler needs. AI Consideration at 41.1% shows that recognition does not consistently convert into selection in individual answers. The management problem is inclusion consistency — not awareness. Softness concentrates in Adventure; Business Travel, Leisure Travel, and Group / Meeting remain stronger. When the hotel is absent, Archer Hotel Falls Church most often appears (1 scenarios).

Why It Matters. If distinctive property attributes are weakly represented, the hotel can look broadly visible while still losing the moments where its real proposition should matter. This is a representation problem first, not automatically a peer-competition program.

Where the Pattern Is Concentrated. Adventure is the softest Scenario Capture at 50.0%, while Business Travel, Leisure Travel, and Group / Meeting show broader coverage. The inclusion issue is concentrated, not universal. Archer Hotel Falls Church appears most often when the hotel is missing (1 scenarios) — use that pattern for source and fact checks, not as proof of cause. Reality Coverage is 25.0% (5 of 20 attributes). Start with gaps that matter operationally — beginning with Airport-Adjacent Location.

What Management Should Focus On Now. Focus first on Outdoor Event Space. Verify first-party and major travel-source completeness for that attribute before treating the issue as a peer-competition problem. Confirm the attribute is stated clearly where AI systems are most likely to read it.

What Not to Overreact To. No comparable prior official period is available — read these as current levels, not period-over-period change.

What to Review Next. Open Reality Gap evidence for Outdoor Event Space and compare recognition cues with official property pages and high-authority travel sources. Then check a small set of related demand scenarios for whether the attribute appears when competitors are named.

Broader Scenario Presence (97.9%) and Consideration (41.1%) do not, by themselves, prove the distinctive attribute is traveling into answers.

biggestConstraint.headline: Not appearing consistently in AI answers

positiveSignal.title: Positive Signal
positiveSignal.body: Among AI answers where hotel ranking could be measured, Falls Church Marriott Fairview Park appeared in the Top 3 100% of the time. This shows how prominently the hotel is positioned when AI includes it.

secondaryCallout.title: Watch Item
secondaryCallout.body: The hotel appeared in at least one AI answer for 97.9% of the traveler needs we tested, but across all individual AI answers it appeared 41.1% of the time. In practical terms, AI recognizes the hotel as relevant for many types of trips, but a traveler will not consistently see it among the hotel options surfaced.

managementPriority.title: Management Priority
managementPriority.body: Focus first on Outdoor Event Space. Verify first-party and major travel-source completeness for that attribute before treating the issue as a peer-competition problem. Confirm the attribute is stated clearly where AI systems are most likely to read it.
